invariant_construction: A lathe-turned solid of revolution, authored as a stacked profile (pad / ball or bun / neck / collar) and joined to the leg or plinth above by a dowel or by being turned in one with the leg blank. Silhouette is fully described by one revolved curve.
permitted_variation_axes: ball vs bun vs onion vs trumpet vs toupie silhouette; overall height; max diameter; ring count and pitch in the collar; pad/disc diameter and thickness; dowel diameter
joints_and_interfaces: dowel into plinth or leg (1984.161 explicit); or turned integral with the leg blank (1954.151, unresolved at web resolution); castor socket bored in the pad (69.146.1)
incompatible_excluded: FC-08-69_140ab and FC-10-1971_281 - their 'foot' is the stile running past the lower rail to the floor, NOT a turned solid. FC-04-1972_47 and FC-03-30_120_5 - carved figural. FC-12-2002_298 - spun metal.
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - no turned-solid donor exists in the library; rough_hewn_timber_beam_v1 is hewn, not turned, and shares no lathe logic
objects_unlocked: chair, stool, chest, bed, table, cabinet - the widest-reaching single recipe in the corpus
unresolved_blockers: No underside view on any member; dowel vs integral turning unresolved on 1954.151 (recorded INFERRED and therefore zero production weight)

invariant_construction: NOT a separate part. The vertical member (stile, post or leg) continues past the lowest rail and terminates on the floor. Authoring this as a foot at all is the error; it is a termination treatment on the post recipe.
permitted_variation_axes: length below the lowest rail; toe radius or wear rounding; splay/cant angle; optional slight pad flare (1969.262)
joints_and_interfaces: none - continuous stock. Interface is the lower rail mortise above it.
incompatible_excluded: every turned-foot member; attaching a turned foot here would require cutting the stile, changing its joint schedule
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - candidate rough_hewn_timber_beam_v1 for the continuous-stock logic only; silhouette, section and interfaces NOT compared
unresolved_blockers: 2011.3 front feet described as integral but the seam is not resolvable in published views

invariant_construction: A sculpted animal terminal (claw-and-ball, paw) carved in the solid at the leg foot. Not generable from a revolved profile.
permitted_variation_axes: scale; toe/talon count; disc pad diameter under a paw; forward rake
joints_and_interfaces: carved integral with the leg blank
incompatible_excluded: all turned and all integral-termination members
unresolved_blockers: 1972.47 notes the disc pad IS separable and reusable alone - a possible sub-part rescue

invariant_construction: A short rectangular block below a cuff at the bottom of a tapered leg. Prismatic, not revolved.
permitted_variation_axes: block height; cuff reed count; taper match to the leg above
joints_and_interfaces: continuous with the leg; cuff is an applied moulding run
unresolved_blockers: single-member family - the split may be an artefact of one object

invariant_construction: A spun gilt-brass ring/torus seated on a stone plinth. Metal fabrication, not joinery.
permitted_variation_axes: lathe profile of the spreading torus; flare ratio; lappet count; bead pitch
joints_and_interfaces: sits on the plinth as a separate spun element
incompatible_excluded: all wood families - different material AND different process
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - forged_iron_v1 is a MATERIAL, not a spun-metal geometry donor
unresolved_blockers: individual ring boundaries not countable in published views

invariant_construction: Square-section vertical carrying the case; mortised on two adjacent faces to receive rails; runs full height corner to corner; face may be reeded, fluted or left plain.
permitted_variation_axes: height; square section width; flute/reed count on exposed faces; roundel-block count interrupting the reeding; whether the post projects above the cornice
joints_and_interfaces: mortise-and-tenon to rails on two faces; groove for panels where frame-and-panel
incompatible_excluded: post.panel_muntin (non-structural, no rail mortises on two faces); post.bed_stacked_block (a stacked assembly, not one stick)
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - candidate rough_hewn_timber_beam_v1 for square-section stock; section, joints and editability NOT compared
objects_unlocked: chest of drawers, wardrobe, desk, cabinet
unresolved_blockers: rear faces unphotographed on 69.146.2 and 2019.59

invariant_construction: Intermediate vertical dividing a framed opening into bays. Grooved on BOTH long edges for panels. Carries no case load; its count is the design parameter.
permitted_variation_axes: count (0 muntins = single-panel front, 2 = three bays, 3 = four bays); width; section; whether it carries applied spindles or ornament
joints_and_interfaces: stub tenon into upper and lower rails; groove both edges
incompatible_excluded: post.case_corner_structural - a corner post is grooved/mortised on adjacent faces, a muntin on opposite faces. Different joint schedule, not a size change.
unresolved_blockers: none material

invariant_construction: A tall post built as an ORDERED STACK of discrete blocks and turnings (plinth block, carved floral block, stepped ring, bead-and-reel band, inlaid rosette square, shaft). The stack ORDER is the recipe; the segments are separate authored parts.
permitted_variation_axes: stack order and segment count; total height (1954.151 proves head and foot posts are the same recipe differing ONLY in height); face width; rosette-cell placement
joints_and_interfaces: segments stacked and presumably pinned or threaded; bed-bolt interface to the side rails
incompatible_excluded: post.case_corner_structural - that is one stick with applied treatment; this is an assembly of separately authored solids
unresolved_blockers: internal fixing between segments never visible; bed-bolt detail unresolved

invariant_construction: A free-standing turned upright whose whole silhouette is one revolved profile, carrying a rail or slab above.
permitted_variation_axes: diameter relative to neighbouring legs; count along a side; presence at all (a 6-leg table drops the medial posts); segment order for the pedestal shaft
joints_and_interfaces: pivot bearing (gate-leg medial post); stacked on plinth (pedestal)
unresolved_blockers: pedestal internal tie rod ASSERTED not seen - recorded INFERRED, zero weight

invariant_construction: A wide flat splayed board acting as a trestle end support, with applied carved layers that can be removed to leave a plain standard.
permitted_variation_axes: height; splay angle; board width; taper; applied-ornament on/off
joints_and_interfaces: housed to the stretcher; carries the frieze carcase above
incompatible_excluded: all square-section and all turned posts
unresolved_blockers: single-member family

invariant_construction: A short upright rising off the seat rail to carry an arm rail. Two sub-shapes co-occur in one object (30.120.59: a tapered front cone-stump AND a wide flat rear post), so the family is defined by ROLE plus a shape parameter, not by one silhouette.
permitted_variation_axes: front-vs-rear shape selector; height; taper; facet count; whether it is continuous with the back frame above (2012.216) or terminates at the arm rail
joints_and_interfaces: tenon into seat rail below, into arm rail above
unresolved_blockers: 2012.216's rear support is explicitly NOT continuous with the back stile - a divergence from the baseline that must not be smoothed over

invariant_construction: Four rails tenoned into legs/posts forming a CLOSED rectangle that carries upholstery. Front and side rails may be show faces; the rear rail is routinely secondary wood.
permitted_variation_axes: length and depth per side; show vs secondary finish per rail (2011.3 proves the rear rail differs from the front on the SAME object); whether the lower edge is straight or cut to an apron profile; peg count
joints_and_interfaces: mortise-and-tenon, pinned with round pegs (30.120.59 visible); corner glue blocks inside
incompatible_excluded: rail.drawer_divider (spans a case, not a seat); rail.frame_and_panel (grooved for panels)
unresolved_blockers: FC-01-1999_488 rear seat rail is NOT DETERMINABLE - no rear or underside view exists. FC-01-2012_216 seat rails are INFERRED FROM TYPE and carry zero production weight.

invariant_construction: A horizontal blade spanning the case front between corner posts or partitions, separating drawer openings. Front edge carries a reed or moulding; count drives drawer count.
permitted_variation_axes: count (drives drawer count); length; height; front-edge profile; whether grooved for bottom boards or mortised for a lock
joints_and_interfaces: tenoned into corner posts and interior partitions
objects_unlocked: chest of drawers, desk, sideboard, chest
unresolved_blockers: runner/guide/stop geometry behind the blade never visible on any member

invariant_construction: Upper and lower rails GROOVED on the inner edge to receive a floating panel, tenoned to stiles and muntins. The groove is the defining feature.
permitted_variation_axes: length; width; how many panel openings the rail spans; groove depth
joints_and_interfaces: mortise-and-tenon to stiles, pegged; groove for panel
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - structural_oak_door_v1 is a MATERIAL asset, not a frame-and-panel geometry donor; do not treat the name as evidence

evidence_classes_present: INFERRED FROM TYPE; NOT DETERMINABLE; PARTIALLY VISIBLE; VISIBLE

permitted_variation_axes: sweep curve; whether it terminates in a scroll, a ram's head or an arcade; arch count in lockstep with spindle count (1999.488); section (round reeded rod vs flat board)

invariant_construction: A long rail spanning head to foot post, thick, sawn from a wide board; may be bowed in plan and serpentine in elevation. Structural core is bare wood with ornament applied.
permitted_variation_axes: length (227 cm on 69.146.1); height; bow amount in plan; count of moulding members on top and bottom edges; ornament applied vs plain
joints_and_interfaces: bed-bolt or hook into the posts (never visible in any view)
unresolved_blockers: the post-to-rail fixing is the single most important unresolved joint in the corpus

invariant_construction: Small-section rail mortised at a regular pitch to receive a spindle gallery above it, or capping that gallery.
permitted_variation_axes: length; mortise pitch for the spindles; whether the face carries a bead run
joints_and_interfaces: mortised for spindles; tenoned to posts
objects_unlocked: bedstead; would extend to settee and cabinet galleries
unresolved_blockers: single-object family (three rails on one bed)

invariant_construction: A rail that PIVOTS, swinging out to carry a fly leg and support a leaf. Requires a hinge/knuckle interface absent from every other rail family.
permitted_variation_axes: swing length; depth; pivot offset from the rail end
joints_and_interfaces: knuckle joint or pivot pin at one end
incompatible_excluded: every fixed rail family - the moving interface is a construction difference, not a parameter
objects_unlocked: side table (game table); would extend to any drop-leaf
unresolved_blockers: knuckle geometry not resolvable; alt7 shows it extended but not the joint

invariant_construction: ONE stick doing both stile and leg: runs unbroken from crest or cornice height down through the seat/case frame to the floor. This is the baseline chair's defining grammar.
permitted_variation_axes: rake angle of the upper portion; section (square vs board-like); taper amount; whether it terminates in its own square foot or continues to a base moulding
joints_and_interfaces: mortised on two faces for rails at multiple heights
incompatible_excluded: FC-01-2012_216 - its rear support is explicitly a SHORT SEPARATE TURNED LEG, not continuous. FC-09-1954_151 - all four corners are the same turned leg master.

unresolved_blockers: FC-01-1999_488 - the junction is masked by the seat rail and gilding, so continuity is PARTIALLY VISIBLE only and recorded at half weight

invariant_construction: The rear support is a SEPARATE member, not continuous with anything above. Often the same blank as the front leg with decoration suppressed (1969.262: identical blank, inlay omitted on the unseen face).
permitted_variation_axes: whether ornament is suppressed on the rear elevation; block schedule; turning profile shared with the front leg
joints_and_interfaces: tenon into seat/case rails only

invariant_construction: Deliberately plain rear member, board-like, notched rather than moulded, because the rear is unseen. Its plainness is the design intent, not a loss of evidence.
permitted_variation_axes: board width; notch depth and shape; total length (300 cm floor-to-tester on 69.146.1)
joints_and_interfaces: housed or nailed to the case; canopy support at the head
unresolved_blockers: none material

invariant_construction: A triangular or quarter block glued into the inside corner of a rail frame. Two mating faces set by the angle of the members it joins.
permitted_variation_axes: block depth; the two mating face angles (1969.262 mates to a CURVED apron, so the recipe needs a curved-face variant)
joints_and_interfaces: glued, sometimes screwed, to two rail faces
incompatible_excluded: brace.structural_gusset (a show member); brace.lid_cleat (a board, not a block)

invariant_construction: A flat sawn board cut to a curve (arch-pierced gusset, cyma bracket, shaped console), left visible and finished to match. A 2D profile swept to constant thickness.
permitted_variation_axes: triangle or cyma proportions; piercing radius and count; span, rise and thickness all free
joints_and_interfaces: glued and pegged between two members; on 1954.151 drilled with weight-reduction holes

invariant_construction: A batten fixed across the underside of a lid to resist cupping and locate the lid on the carcase.
permitted_variation_axes: cleat width; fixing pattern (pegs vs screws); whether moulded to match the lid edge
joints_and_interfaces: pegged or screwed to the lid underside
unresolved_blockers: 1971.281's cleats are a LATER REPAIR in pale unpatinated wood with modern slotted screws - explicitly not original, and must not be treated as period evidence

invariant_construction: A metal arm controlling or supporting a moving element (quadrant stay for a fall front; an internal tie rod).
permitted_variation_axes: arc radius and chord (set by fall depth); strap width; sliding vs fixed upper end
joints_and_interfaces: pivots on the carcase stile; slides in a slot
sinc_donor_candidate: AUDIT_REQUIRED - forged_iron_v1 is a MATERIAL, not a stay geometry donor

invariant_construction: The joined grammar stile-muntin-...-stile crossed by upper and lower rails, all pegged, grooved throughout to receive floating panels. Bay count is the parameter; the JOINT SCHEDULE is the invariant.
permitted_variation_axes: bay count and proportion; stile/rail widths; muntin count; groove depth; whether the frame receives applied ornament or is left plain
joints_and_interfaces: mortise-and-tenon, pegged; continuous groove
incompatible_excluded: frame.applied_moulded_surround (an applied margin, no groove, carries no panel structurally)

invariant_construction: Concentric stepped/reeded margins applied to a flat carcase face, shrinking inward to a flat field. Not a joined frame - a moulding layout on a board.
permitted_variation_axes: aperture width and height; number of steps in the ovolo/cove stack; corner treatment (plain mitre throughout on 69.146.1)
joints_and_interfaces: glued/pinned to the carcase face; mitred at corners

invariant_construction: There is NO frame part. What reads as a frame is the ASSEMBLY of post + post + bottom rail + crest. Authoring a frame object here would duplicate members already modelled.
permitted_variation_axes: n/a - the parameters belong to the member recipes
joints_and_interfaces: the members' own joints
unresolved_blockers: none - this family exists to PREVENT a modelling error, not to be built

invariant_construction: A board seated loose in the surrounding frame groove, free to move. Blank is separable from its face treatment: a plain, a carved and a marquetry panel are the SAME blank.
permitted_variation_axes: aspect ratio; thickness; flat vs raised/fielded; bevel depth; shouldered vs rectangular raised field; face treatment swapped independently of the blank

invariant_construction: A textile field set within a show-wood lip: foundation + padding + cover, crowned. Occupies the panel SLOT but shares no construction with a wooden panel.
permitted_variation_axes: field size; padding crown height; edge roll; whether both faces are upholstered (1999.488 is upholstered on BOTH faces of the back frame)

permitted_variation_axes: section swap (chamfer / ovolo / cavetto / roll / astragal / thumbnail / multi-reed / stepped ogee); run length; mitre vs stopped ends; scale
joints_and_interfaces: applied and mitred

invariant_construction: A discrete carved or cast CELL instanced at a regular pitch along a path (bead-and-reel, rosette chain, wave scroll, lappet register). Generator is instance-along-curve, not sweep.
permitted_variation_axes: cell pitch; cell selection; run length; register count; whether the run is straight or follows a curve
joints_and_interfaces: applied along an edge
unresolved_blockers: individual cell boundaries not countable on 2002.298

invariant_construction: ONE hand-authored relief master instanced many times with only placement transforms. The master itself is bespoke; the INSTANCING is the recipe.

invariant_construction: A small set of flat cut-veneer masters (blossom, serrated leaf, stem) composed into a scrolling field. 69.146.3 states the field is built from roughly THREE masters.
